Qaid V Muk Gayi Kazim Nu Koi Rowan Te Aaye
Baghdad De Lokaan Ne Naa Tauq Lahaye.

1
Musa Kazim Da Koi Aisa Dardi Howay.
Sain Masooma Nu Ja Khabar Aye Sunaway.
Bhaina Nu Madine Toon Tu Lay Rowan Layi Aaye.
Pori Dunya Andar Iko Kofa Hoya.

2
Jithe Wasday Lokaan Nayi Ik Janaza Chaya.
Iss Shehar De Wich Lashay Mazdoraan Ne Chaye.
Sham Toon Bad Nayi Qatal Gah Ban Gayi Aye.
Pul Te Rahi Maiyyat Eho Payi Aakhdi Aye.

3
Koi Aal-e-Muhammad Choo Baghdad Na Jaye.
Eho Hasrat Mula Tere Akbar Di Aye.
Sain Zahra Nu Enj Tera Ohh Pursa Deway.
Baghdad Walay Pul Te Taboot Uthaye.

p = Path(\"src/data/lyrics/qaid-v-muk-gayi-kazim-nu-koi-rowan-te-lyrics-2018-tajpoints-c58c7170c95b66b40808.md\")
_, metadata, body = p.read_text().split(\"---\", 2)
roman = metadata.split(\"romanLyrics: |-\\n\", 1)[1]
groups = lambda s: [block.splitlines() for block in s.strip().split(\"\\n\\n\")]
r, b = groups(roman), groups(body)
assert [len(g) for g in r] == [len(g) for g in b] == [2, 5, 5, 5]
assert [g[0].strip() for g in r[1:]] == list(\"123\")

assert \"\\u200c\" not in body
print(\"Verified two preamble verses and three four-verse stanzas in both editions.\")

item.text:
Reconstructed the selected lyric in Shahmukhi Punjabi and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. Both editions have a two-verse preamble and three four-verse stanzas.

Updated the language metadata based on Punjabi grammar throughout the poem. In stanza 2, I read the ambiguous Roman `nayi` as `نئیں` (“didn’t”) in the first verse and `نئی` (“new”) in the third.
